title: Timed open cloze
summary: Use a complete-passage first pass, a targeted second pass and a final read to solve open cloze accurately under time pressure.

sections.title: Protect accuracy when the clock is running
content: Recall the four evidence checks from E4.1–E4.4: sentence structure, controlling word form, lexical fit and paragraph cohesion. A timed passage can test all four in any order.
Your target is eight gaps in eight minutes. Speed comes from postponing uncertain gaps and returning with more context, not from guessing before you have read the passage.

sections.title: Use the first-pass, second-pass, final-read routine
content: First pass — about four minutes: read the title and complete passage, then fill only answers you can justify immediately. Mark every uncertain gap and keep moving.
Second pass — about three minutes: classify each remaining gap as grammar, form, vocabulary or cohesion. Inspect the words on both sides and at least one neighbouring sentence before choosing.
Final read — about one minute: reread the completed passage without stopping. Check reference chains, tense sequence, fixed expressions and whether every answer is exactly one word.

sections.title: Spend time according to evidence
content: A fixed frame such as “divide the route ___ three sections” is a first-pass item because divide into supplies strong immediate evidence.
A connector after “The water looked clear” must be checked against the next action. Collecting a sample despite that appearance creates contrast, so but or yet fits the meaning.
A word such as again is not proved by grammar alone. It becomes secure only when an earlier sentence records the first count.
In “the data would be useless ___ every group used the same method”, test the completed meaning. Unless preserves the teacher's condition; if reverses it.

sections.title: Run a three-pass rehearsal
content: Set an eight-minute countdown. At four minutes, leave every unresolved gap blank and begin the second pass. This prevents one difficult item from consuming the whole task.
Beside each delayed gap, write one label: grammar, form, vocabulary or cohesion. State the evidence aloud before entering the answer.
At seven minutes, stop solving individual gaps and begin the final read. Record which pass produced each correction so you can improve your time allocation.

sections.title: Complete the hillside water survey
content: Read the whole five-paragraph account before committing to difficult answers. Complete its eight gaps in eight minutes using the three-pass routine.
The passage mixes fixed structures, contrast, reference, repetition and tense sequence. No word bank is provided, and every response must contain exactly one word.

sections.title: Audit both answers and timing
content: Premature guess: I answered before reading enough of the passage.
Stalled first pass: I spent too long on one uncertain gap instead of moving on.
Evidence mismatch: my word fitted locally but failed the grammar, meaning or cohesion check.
Missing final read: I left an agreement, tense, reference or one-word-format error that a complete reread could have caught.

sections.title: The hillside water survey
content: Complete one original eight-gap module checkpoint in eight minutes. Submit only after the final read; feedback appears for the complete passage after submission.
